issues.description: Directory/check name and CHANGELOG say 'single_network_interface' but PR title/description say 'multiple_network_interfaces'
issues.detail: The PR title and description refer to detecting VMs with multiple network interfaces, but the actual check ID, directory name, file names, and CHANGELOG entry all use 'compute_instance_single_network_interface'. This is internally consistent in the diff, but the metadata Recommendation.Url 'hub.prowler.com/check/compute_instance_single_network_interface' must match the registered check ID. Confirm the intended slug before merge to avoid a broken docs link or rename later.

issues.description: GKE prefix heuristic is brittle and easily bypassed or false-positive
issues.detail: Marking any instance whose name starts with 'gke-' as MANUAL relies on naming convention only. Users can name non-GKE VMs starting with 'gke-' to silence findings, and GKE node names can vary. Consider detecting GKE membership via labels (e.g., 'goog-gke-node') or metadata rather than name prefix, and document the heuristic's limits in metadata Notes.

When interface_count is 0, report.status remains 'PASS' from the default initialization, but status_extended says the instance has no interfaces. A VM with zero NICs is an unusual/edge state and arguably not a 'pass' for a network-interface posture check. Either treat as INFO/MANUAL or explicitly justify why zero is PASS; current behavior is confusing and untested.

issues.description: Mutable default argument on Pydantic field
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a mutable default. Pydantic BaseModel handles this safely at instantiation, but the surrounding model uses the same pattern for other lists, so it's consistent. Consider `Field(default_factory=list)` for clarity and to avoid future foot-guns if anyone migrates off Pydantic semantics.

issues.description: No test coverage for zero-interface or empty-name edge cases
issues.detail: The test suite covers 0 instances, 1 NIC, 2 NICs, 3 NICs, mixed, and GKE — but not the empty network_interfaces list branch (lines 35-38 in the check) nor the case where interface.get('name', '') returns ''. Adding one test for each would lock in the intended behavior of the 'else' branch and the GKE name heuristic boundary (e.g. 'gke-' prefix on non-GKE VM).

issues.description: NetworkInterface class defined after Instance references it
issues.detail: `NetworkInterface` is declared on line 606 but `Instance` (line 628) references it via type annotation `list[NetworkInterface]`. With `from __future__ import annotations` or string annotations this works; otherwise Pydantic may complain at class-definition time. Verify the file's import semantics or move the NetworkInterface class above Instance for clarity and forward-compatibility.

review.summary: The check is straightforward and well-tested for the happy paths, but two issues stand out before merge. First, the naming inconsistency: the PR description talks about detecting 'multiple network interfaces' while everything in code/metadata/CHANGELOG is named 'single_network_interface' — confirm the intended slug since metadata.Recommendation.Url depends on it. Second, the GKE detection uses a brittle name-prefix heuristic ('gke-') that can be bypassed by naming and may miss legitimate GKE nodes; using labels would be more robust. The zero-interface branch silently passes without a test. Minor cleanups around mutable defaults and forward class references round out the review.
